generated_for: Trimcraft official leftover named model catalog

models.name: Rich Fish
models.description: This little puppy is based on the tradition of the classic Keel Fish championed by Rich Pavel for decades. When people say there is something different about Rich’s boards, they aren’t lying — the sheer amount of hidden curves and refined touches that are packed into roughly 5 feet of surfboard is nothing short of magic. Extreme down the line speed on less than impressive waves is the staple of the classic Keel Fish, but hold on to your shorts when that epic day comes, these Rich Fishes are more capable in real surf than you’d ever imagine.

models.name: Sidecut Keel
models.description: Think classic keel paddle, with a more seamless transition onto rail. Lots of projection and glide as you’d expect from a fishy outline. The subtle acceleration of the outline curve reduces the surface area under your back foot and modernizes the feel compared to a classic fish. More ability to square-up off the bottom and a more seamless on-rail transitions as well as easier to surf on your backhand.

models.name: Wills Fish
models.description: The model that was too fun NOT to be! William Aliotti and Ryan Lovelace started off on this shape as a travel fish bound for Indo and beyond; what resulted was an extremely fun high-performance twin that seems as comfortable in onshore European slop as it does in standup Indo tubes. We decided to throw this model into the Trimcraft mix as we opened up shop in Florida with Mike Whisnant and Derek Jackson – something for the softer, quicker waves that fits between your shortboard and a keel fish; still plenty of volume, but refined in the tips to stay sensitive and not fight your transitions between shortboard and alternative. Airs, tubes, slop, slashes…Covered!

models.name: Davey Fish
models.description: Modeled after Davey’s 1970’s pro model twins, this is a true to form channeled twin with some super modern updates. The modifications lay mainly in rocker, fin placement and bottom contour that the channels are set into; all refined from the decades of knowledge gained since the original variations, these little guys will generate tons of speed over flats and have you twinning all over mushy beach and reef breaks, or shooting down the line at your local point. Super loose, super fast, SUPER fun little water skates, developed from decades of experience, usually surfed from the high 5′ up into the low to mid 6′ range in length; size it about two inches longer than your average twin keel fish.

models.name: Symmetrical Snake
models.description: With more surface area forward and a slightly higher volume than a regular shortboard, the Symmetrical Snake is a high-lift, low drag vehicle. A single concave running all the way from the nose all the way through the tail and a modern shortboard rail line and rocker make the Symmetrical Snake far more appropriate board for average-to-good days than the standard chip. Shaped with either squash (quick pumps and beachbreaks), round (bowly reefs, points and heavy carving) or swallow tails (skate and flow in all conditions).

models.name: T. Rev
models.description: Think high-volume quad fish in the front two thirds, with a pulled-in round tail. A proven Lovelace classic originally designed for Trevor Gordon. Very flat rocker, flat deck with down rails and a vee to double, into single afterburner concave bottom. Tons of skate off the middle & enough curve to hold that power through turns – These sleds like chunky beachbreaks and bowly reefs, even though they cut their teeth on Santa Barbara’s small point surf. In other words, enjoy all over!

models.name: Haley Pin
models.description: The best way to mentally approach this mid length is to take a classic double-ender mini glider vibe, then send it into hyperdrive with an extremely technical triplane bottom shape – to be specific, a vee under the nose – into double concave, spiral vee, then that signature flat spot just behind the fin – all packed between those trippy flat chines that break the water flow for quick planing and even quicker transitions onto rail. So all that is to say, extremely versatile in small and average surf, will cheater-5 til the end of the world, with an exceptionally positive response off the back foot. Based on the Lovelace ThickLizzy – these things are quickly becoming quiver staples all over the world.

models.name: Lopez Single
models.description: An extremely clean 70’s era outline style that screams classic. Repeat, classic. This may look like one you’ve seen before, but beware of assumptions — the Lopez tradition is mired in clean, subtle curves and beautifully tucked edges. More rocker than the original old school singles with an updated rail shape, but fully in-step with that classic 70’s flow. Impossible to go wrong!

models.name: Power Cat
models.description: Decode that model name and you’ve got it! A ‘Power Cat’ in boating terms, is a powered twin hull. Full displacement hull foil nose to tail, these blades are meant to scream with relative ease. The twin fin variation gets them on rail quicker, and with more forgiveness than the average single fin hull – much better suited to the average surfer and average waves, but still plenty foiled to satisfy the seasoned hull-head’s need for knife-edge trim speed. Best between 6’10 and 8′.

models.name: Diamond Twin
models.description: Originally designed for his friend Temple and realized it was missing from his personal quiver, it’s a nice middle ground between a mid length for drawn out smooth surfing and and shorter boards for staying in the pocket. keeping a little bit longer rail line paired with a sightly pulled in nose and at the wing a bit of an accelerated tail rocker with V to help keep the board agile under the back foot and make it a little easier for top to bottom surfing.

models.name: Burner
models.description: A shortboard for those of us who don’t ‘shortboard’. An extremely versatile board for travel and daily driver use – the Burner has found loving homes under the feet of slop-surfing weekend warriors and globe-trotting barrel hunters alike. A slightly forward wide-point gives you tons of flow and glide, but the modernized rocker curve and foil produce a positive, responsive and forgiving experience. Designed by Ryan Lovelace, this is one of the most popular boards in our line around the world.

models.name: Re.bowls
models.description: A versatile down-railed egg based on Ryan Lovelace’s magical midlength, the v.Bowls. The re.Bowls was designed to surf a variety of waves the v.Bowls is often put away for: the average, shifty, mushy, knee to head high surf — better for forward trim and making flat sections than its rounder counterpart, the re.Bowls offers an accessibility to that effortless singlefin glide with a kinder learning curve.

models.name: Big Pin
models.description: Trimcraft’s first longboard offering – something for the logger who thought they had everything. The BigPin is a hybridized longboard & glider, suited for all kinds of waves, especially for those of us who enjoy the super-glibe of a longboard but aren’t out to hang heels and dance the tip; More apt to arcing carves and swooping around the face with connectivity usually lost on a traditional log, while still very capable and happy to keep you cheating-five all day long. The origins of this model can be traced back to a down-rail longboard shape instigated by Cyrus Sutton and shaped by Lovelace – though this new iteration borrows from Ryan’s past few years refining a bottom shape that gets bigger boards onto rail like silk. Arcing, cruising, cheating, the BigPin is it!
